title: Interactive drift explorer and automated triage runbook for throughput/p95 regressions
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: Provide an end-to-end workflow for surfacing, inspecting, and resolving tokens/sec and latency (p95) regressions across load harness runs. Deliverables: 1) compact time-series + trace retention schema for long-tail raw run data (optimized for delta queries by cohort), 2) a queryable diff explorer UI that supports cohort selection, aligned token/time normalization, and annotated regression fingerprints, and 3) an automated triage runbook that can be kicked off from the UI and attaches evidence bundles (PRs, playback requests, heatmaps) to a Linear incident.

Scope and constraints: We must keep storage costs bounded (target < 20% of current bench storage growth) while preserving enough raw KV cache + latency traces for root-cause. The UI must load diffs for a 24h window in < 2s for typical cohorts (<= 1000 traces). Integration points: bench-ingest pipeline, benchmark-result-store, reg-alert service, console rollouts dashboard.

Design notes (high level):
- Data model: keep two tiers: compact-timeseries (per-run aggregates: tokens/sec, p50, p95, failure-rate, sample-count, model-variant, seqlen-distribution-hash) and hot-trace-reservoir (bounded sample of raw event traces with metadata for replay).
- Fingerprinting: use deterministic run fingerprint computed from model-hash + config + stable-seed + cohort-signature, store as indexed string for fast diff joins.
- Diffing: compute pairwise delta on tokens/sec and p95, normalize for input-length and batch-size, surface effect-size + regression-score (statistical + practical threshold).
- UI: left pane cohort selector + filters (model, region, runtime, input-type); middle pane delta table with sparklines; right pane focused evidence: heatmap, top contributing traces, candidate PRs.
- Triage runbook automation: auto-generate hypothesis checklist, suggested follow-ups (run playback at 1.5x load, compare kernel variant), and pre-populated Linear ticket template with attached evidence bundle and recommended assignees.

Success criteria: detect 95% of previously-known regressions from historical archive, median triage time reduced from ~3.2h to <= 1.0h, UI queries meet SLAs, storage growth stays within target.

Open decisions: storage retention policy for hot-trace-reservoir (30d vs 90d), default cohort granularity (route vs request-signature), whether to materialize pre-computed pairwise diffs nightly or compute on-demand.

2025-11-14 - Aisha Kapoor: Architecture spike complete. Prototype of compact-timeseries schema in bench-store-migrations branch. Uploaded schema DDL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-store/compare/compact-schema
2025-11-15 - Laura Bennett (PM): Reviewed scope; asked to prioritize triage automation before full UI polish to reduce MTTR for customer-facing incidents.

2025-11-16 - Aisha Kapoor: Implemented fingerprinting function and ingest hook. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/412 (WIP). Observed fingerprint collisions for some cohort signatures; plan to include sequence-length-plus-hash to reduce collisions.
2025-11-18 - Ops (SRE): Flagged potential cold-start latency when retrieving hot-trace-reservoir for large cohorts. Proposal: add rate-limited reservoir retrieval API and paginated trace streaming.

2025-11-19 - Marco Chen: Added draft triage-playbook.md to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b-triage-playbook (contains checkpoint checklist, replay commands, and suggested alert thresholds).
2025-11-20 - Aisha Kapoor: Wireframes uploaded to Figma and shared with Design (link below). Starting backend iteration: compact-timeseries write path and index on fingerprint+run_ts.
2025-11-20 - Design (Chloe Park): Quick UI review - recommend reducing default columns and adding a 'quick-replay' button on hover for top traces to speed triage.
next_steps: 1) Finish compact-timeseries write path and create index on fingerprint by 2025-11-22. 2) Implement reservoir API and sampling enforcement (2025-11-25). 3) Build minimal diff compute service (on-demand first) and hook into reg-alert to emit enriched alerts (2025-11-28).
blocked_by: Pending final decision on hot-trace retention policy and SRE capacity for paginated trace API rollout.
note_for_reviewers: Reviewers: focus on data model DDL (compact-timeseries) and reservoir sampling algorithm — we want deterministic reproducible samples across replays. Call out any costs you expect in storage or query latency.
postmortem_examples: Incident ENG-44567: tokens/sec regression due to kernel fallback (linked evidence) - this workflow should have surfaced the regression with a clear kernel delta signature.
Incident ENG-92011: p95 drift after quantization profile change - aim to reduce false positives by normalizing seqlen distribution in diffs.
